claim: On 2025-11-20 Application Load Balancers launched Target Optimizer, which enforces a maximum number of concurrent requests on a target with an agent that runs on the targets; its traffic generates more LCU usage than regular target groups.
question: What is ALB Target Optimizer and how does it change the bill?

values.display: enforce a maximum number of concurrent requests

evidence.quote: Application Load Balancer (ALB) now offers Target Optimizer, a new feature that allows you to enforce a maximum number of concurrent requests on a target.
Once enabled, the feature works with the help of an agent provided by AWS that you run on your targets that tracks request concurrency.
Traffic to target groups that enable Target Optimizer generates more LCU usage than regular target groups.

note: d132. Current truth: elb-alb-target-optimizer-no-sticky-more-lcu. The FAQ gives the Target Optimizer LCU sizes (numbers lens).

claim: On 2026-09-03 Gateway Load Balancers added optional TCP Reset packets when a target becomes unhealthy, is deregistered, or a flow's idle timeout expires; before, existing TCP connections kept going to the unhealthy target (fail-open). It is off by default.
question: What did the Gateway Load Balancer TCP Reset option change, and is it examinable?

values.display: TCP Reset is not enabled by default

evidence.quote: AWS Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) now supports sending TCP Reset (RST) packets when a target becomes unhealthy, is deregistered, or when a flow's idle timeout expires.
Previously, when a GWLB target failed, existing TCP connections would continue to be forwarded to the unhealthy target (aka fail-open behavior).
TCP Reset is not enabled by default to ensure backward compatibility.

changed.was: existing TCP connections would continue to be forwarded to the unhealthy target (aka fail-open behavior)

note: d131. Not examinable yet (after the 2026-07-15 cutoff).
